name: Greek black-figure pottery
summary: Greek vases in which the painter draws figures in a black gloss slip on the red clay and cuts the details with a sharp point. A three-stage firing makes the black and the red.

philosophy.core_thesis: A pot is a surface for story: black silhouettes on red clay, made sharp with incised lines, tell a myth in frieze after frieze.
design_principles: Paint each figure as a solid black silhouette in gloss slip on the red clay.
Incise the inner lines of the figures with a sharp point to show the red clay below.
Add purple-red and white slip for flesh of women, hair, and clothing accents.
Divide the pot into panels and friezes that run round the body in horizontal bands.
Fire in three stages: oxidation, reduction and re-oxidation, at 800 to 950 °C.
Keep the main scene on the shoulder or the belly, and a lotus and palmette band below the handles.
Write the name of the painter or the potter in a short line on the vase, when it is signed.
anti_patterns: Red figures on a black ground
Soft shading or colour blends inside the figure
A glaze that covers the whole pot with a clear gloss
A thick wall with no foot and no clear profile

form.shape: Amphorae, kraters, hydriai and kylikes with a clear division into foot, belly, shoulder, neck and lip.
form.profile: The profile is a taut S-curve; an amphora has an ovoid body and a narrow neck, and a kylix has a shallow bowl on a stem.
form.foot_and_rim: A flared or stepped foot, a flat or spreading lip, and two vertical handles that join the neck and the shoulder.
form.proportion: Height 25 to 60 cm, wall 3 to 6 mm, and the foot diameter about one third of the maximum diameter.
rules: Throw large vases in two or three parts and join them at the neck and the foot.
Keep the wall thin and even; the form is as precise as the painting.
Place the main picture in a rectangular field between the handles.
Leave the underside of the foot as the reserved red clay.

bodies.rule: Use a fine, iron-rich Attic clay that fires to a warm orange-red. Refine the clay by settling until the wall is smooth and thin.

methods: throwing on the wheel in parts
forming.joins: Parts are joined with a thin clay slip; handles are made separately and luted on at the neck and the shoulder.
forming.details: A reserved line at the foot, a glossy black band at the lip, and a light stilt or finger mark where the pot stood in the kiln.

glaze.pattern: Mythic and daily scenes in a frieze, with figures in profile; palmettes and lotus bands fill the zones above and below.
glaze.gloss: The black slip is bright and glassy, about 60 to 80 GU; the red clay is satin.
glaze.wear: The black can flake at the edges and show a dull red-brown; the incised lines stay sharp.

palette.strategy: Two colours that the firing makes, black and red, with small touches of purple-red and white for accent.

firing.kiln: A wood-fired updraught kiln with a fire chamber below the floor of the pots and a vent at the top.
processes: paint the slip on the leather-hard pot
reduction phase with green wood to 950 °C
firing.scale: Workshops in the Kerameikos of Athens had a master potter, several painters and many slaves and apprentices.
firing.signs: A sharp edge between black and red, a small red stain where the black fired in oxidation, and a stilt mark under the foot.

pieces.form: Neck amphora with a panel on each side and a lotus band under the handles
Kylix with a frieze on each side and a Gorgon mask in the tondo
Hydria with three handles and a main field on the shoulder
Column krater with an inner panel on the rim and plain black lower wall

positive: black gloss silhouettes on orange-red clay
museum photograph on a neutral ground

canonical_works.work: Amphora with Achilles and Ajax playing a game

lineage.root: Corinthian potters made it first; no earlier style in this data leads to it.

emotion.target_response: A calm, tense clarity: the viewer sees a story in sharp black shapes and feels the discipline of a trained hand.

use_cases: a museum or educational plate on Greek pottery
a myth scene on a vessel
an amphora or krater in a classical interior prompt
avoid_when: the brief needs figures that look modelled and three-dimensional
the brief needs a glazed colour surface

modifiers.how: Reverse the ground: paint the background black and leave the figures in the red clay, with brush lines for detail.
Keep the fine red clay, remove the figures, and press a relief pattern in a mould.
